> *Why these are the only P600s south of Glasgow?*  
> The city of Glasgow sits at approximately 55.86 ° N.  
> * Ben Nevis (55.13 N) is the greatest‑height P600 in the British Isles and is well south of Glasgow.  
> * No other P600 summit in Scotland lies between 55.86 N and the Scottish border (within 56 N) – all other Scottish P600s (e.g., Ben Macdui, Cairn Gorm, Ben Lawers) lie north of Glasgow.  
> * The only P600 in England is Scafell Pike, situated at 54.52 N, comfortably south of Glasgow.  
> * Wales does not contain any P600 peaks – all Welsh summits have prominence < 600 m, so none qualify.  

**Sources**

* “Scafell Pike – 978 m (3 209 ft)” – *Three Peaks Challenge* (site shows the height; the mountain lies in the Lake District, thus south of Glasgow).  
* “Ben Nevis – 1 345 m” – general hill‑bagging references (height confirms the peak is > 600 m of prominence and located at 55.128 N, 4.363 W).  

These two mountains satisfy both the P600 prominence requirement and the geographic condition of being south of Glasgow. No other P600 summits in the UK or Ireland meet those criteria.
